logStreamUrl: The stream URL with no credential in it. Utils.SSE opens it with credentials so the session cookie is sent.
getLogs: Takes no filter arguments. The backend route accepts severity, component, traceId, limit and cursor query parameters and this function sends none of them.
getTransactions: Sends no status or limit filter, although the backend route accepts both.

decisions.name: AuthCallsUseTheSharedRequestCore
decisions.what: login, logout and validateSession go through API.Request like every other call
why: They used raw fetch while API.Request required a user id for its Bearer header. That requirement is gone.
credentials: Include, set in API.Request, is what lets the browser store the Set-Cookie from login and send the cookie afterwards.

login: POST /auth/login. A successful answer sets the HttpOnly session cookie and returns the session (user id, name, role, capabilities).
A wrong username or password is Refused 401 with the text 'Invalid username or password'. Too many attempts is refused with its own text.
loginRegisterId is always sent as Nothing by Pages.Login.
logout: POST /auth/logout, which answers with no body. Main.signOut ignores the result and signs the browser out locally either way.
validateSession: GET /auth/me. Refused 401 when the browser holds no valid session cookie.
Called once, by Main at boot.

decisions.name: QueryModeDispatchInFetchInventory
decisions.what: fetchInventory dispatches between three data sources by QueryMode: JsonMode (static file), HttpMode (REST API), GqlMode (GraphQL)
why: JsonMode reads ./inventory.json from the app's own origin with a cache-busting timestamp and no credentials.
HttpMode reads the configured apiEndpoint through API.Request.getAbsolute.
GqlMode calls GraphQL.API.Inventory.readInventoryGql and is the default in Config.LiveView.defaultViewConfig.
The mode is a source-level setting. No screen changes it.

fetchInventory: Three-way dispatch on QueryMode; the default is GqlMode per Config.LiveView.defaultViewConfig.
JsonMode and HttpMode are alternatives for development or fallback; the production path is GqlMode.
fetchInventoryFromJson: Reads ./inventory.json from the same origin; relative path means it is served by the same web server as the app.
Appends ?t=<currentTimestamp> for cache-busting; the file might be updated out-of-band.
No auth headers; the file is assumed to be public on the same origin.
deleteInventory: The backend answers 404 'Item not found' for an unknown SKU, which arrives as Refused 404.

getDailyReport: Takes Types.Manager.DailyReportRequest: a DateTime and a location UUID. The backend decodes both and reads neither.
The earlier version sent the text "today" and an empty location id, which the backend could not decode.
getAlerts: Decodes Types.Manager.ManagerAlert, the tagged shape the backend writes.
overrideVoid: Has no caller. Pages.TransactionHistory voids through API.Sale.voidSale.
orActorId is required by the backend's decoder and is not read by the handler.
activityStreamUrl: The stream URL with no credential in it. Has no caller yet.

getRefund: Money fields are RefundMoney (zero or negative cents). Line quantities are RefundQuantity (zero or more).
getAllRefunds: Has no caller. The sales history page lists sales, not refund rows.

decisions.name: RegisterCallsHaveOneCallerEach
decisions.what: createRegister, openRegister and closeRegister are called only by Pages.Registers; getRegister only by Pages.CreateTransaction.load
why: Nothing creates or opens a register as a side effect any more.
The backend requires capCanManageRegisters for create and update, capCanOpenRegister for open and capCanCloseRegister for close. Pages.Registers shows each control by the same capability.

getRegisters: GET /register returns every register. Any signed-in user may call it.
getRegister: Refused 404 'Register not found' for an unknown id.
createRegister: POST /register with a whole Register record. Refused 403 without capCanManageRegisters.
openRegister: POST /register/open/<id> with the starting cash in cents. The opener is the session user.
Refused 409 'Register is already open' for an open register.
closeRegister: POST /register/close/<id> with the counted cash in cents.
The result's variance is the expected drawer amount minus the counted cash. A positive variance means cash is missing.
Refused 409 for a register that is already closed.

decisions.name: OneStatusCheckingCore
decisions.what: Every request goes through one private function, request, which checks the HTTP status before decoding the body
why: It replaced ten near-identical helpers, most of which decoded the body whatever the status was.
A refusal from the backend is usually plain text. Decoding it as JSON turned the backend's message into a parse error.
The public helpers (get, getAbsolute, post, postEmpty, postUnit, put, delete, deleteUnit) differ only in method, body and whether a response body is read.

decisions.name: ErrorsAreTyped
decisions.what: Every helper returns Either ApiError a. ApiError is Refused status body, Unreachable message or Undecodable message
why: The backend answers 400, 403, 404 and 409 with different meanings on sale writes. Screens branch on the status with isRefusal and show the backend's own text with describe.
Unreachable means fetch itself failed (network, CORS, TLS). Undecodable means a 2xx answer whose body did not decode.
UI.Remote.useRemote takes these values and stores describe of the error in RemoteData's Failure.

decisions.name: CookieIsTheOnlyCredential
decisions.what: Requests are sent with credentials: Include and no Authorization header. No API function takes a user id
why: The backend authenticates by the HttpOnly session cookie. Its cookie middleware puts the session token into the Authorization header itself.
The backend refuses a user id in the Authorization header with 401 (nix/sale-checks/auth.sh checks this).
A GET sends only Accept. Content-Type is sent only with a body.

describe: A refusal shows the response body as the backend wrote it. A refusal with an empty body names the HTTP status instead.
Used for every error message the screens show.
isRefusal: True only for Refused with exactly the given status. Unreachable and Undecodable are never a refusal.
status: Just the HTTP status for Refused, Nothing for Unreachable and Undecodable.
postUnit: For routes that answer with no body (POST /auth/logout answers 204). The response body is not read.
postEmpty: POST with no request body and a decoded response. Used by clear, finalize and the stock pull actions.
getAbsolute: Takes a full URL instead of a path under apiBaseUrl. Used for the configured inventory endpoint in HttpMode.

openIssues.name: SessionExpiryIsNotNoticed
openIssues.what: A 401 in the middle of a session is shown as an error message on the page that made the request; the app stays in the signed-in state
why: Main asks for the session once at boot. Nothing watches later responses for 401.
Wanted: a Refused 401 from any request signs the browser out and shows the login page.

decisions.name: ReadsAndManagerOpsOnly
decisions.what: Only getAllSales, getSale, voidSale and refundSale are here; sale building is in API.SaleCommand
why: Callers: Pages.TransactionHistory (getAllSales, voidSale, refundSale), UI.Transaction.CreateTransaction and Services.CurrentSale (getSale).

getAllSales: GET /sale returns every sale of every status. Refund rows are not included.
Any signed-in user may call it.
voidSale: POST /sale/void/<id> with the reason as a JSON string.
Refused 403 without capCanVoidTransaction. Refused 409 for a sale already voided or refunded. The backend checks no ownership.
refundSale: POST /sale/refund/<id> with the reason as a JSON string. The answer is the refund row.
Refused 403 without capCanRefundTransaction. Refused 409 unless the sale is completed and not yet refunded.

openIssues.name: SaleListIsUnbounded
openIssues.what: getAllSales loads every sale ever made in one response
why: The backend route has no paging or date filter. Pages.TransactionHistory sorts and draws the whole list.
Needs a backend change first.

decisions.name: StockCallsUseTheSharedRequestCore
decisions.what: Every stock call goes through API.Request; the module's own fetch helpers are gone
why: The pull actions with no data (accept, start, fulfill, retry) use Request.postEmpty. The backend routes take no request body.
cancel and issue post {irNote}; message posts {nmMessage}.

getQueue: Pages.Stock.Interface passes Just (LocationId dummyLocationId) so it sees only the configured location's queue. See Config.Entity.DummyIdsUsedInProductionCodePaths.
With no locationId and no location on the user account the backend answers 400.
cancelPull: POST with body {irNote: reason}; the backend records the reason as the cancellation note.
Cancellation is terminal; the pull cannot be reopened, only a fresh pull request created.
queueStreamUrl: The stream URL with no credential in it. Utils.SSE opens it with credentials. The backend requires capCanFulfillOrders.

openIssues.name: DummyIdsUsedInProductionCodePaths
openIssues.what: dummyLocationId is a hardcoded UUID that every register, queue read and report request uses as the location; the other dummy ids have no user
why: The session carries no location, so the front end has nowhere else to get one. It is a real foreign key on the backend.
dummyAccountId, dummyPaymentId, dummyTransactionId, dummyEmployeeId and dummyRegisterId are unused since the 2026-10-10 refactor and can be deleted.

dummyLocationId: The one configured location. Used by Pages.Registers (new registers), Pages.Stock.Interface (queue filter) and Pages.Manager.Panels.ReportsPanel (report request).

decisions.name: GqlModeAsDefaultQueryMode
decisions.what: defaultViewConfig.mode = GqlMode; the LiveView page reaches for GraphQL by default rather than REST or static JSON
decisions.why: GraphQL is the most expressive of the three (lets the UI pick exactly the fields it needs). JsonMode is the offline fallback (reads ./inventory.json); HttpMode is the REST path. Changing mode currently requires editing defaultViewConfig source; no runtime switch. See API.Inventory.QueryModeDispatchInFetchInventory for the dispatch logic.

defaultViewConfig: Default sort: Quantity descending, then Category ascending, then Species descending. Multi-field comparator from Types.Inventory.compareMenuItems.
hideOutOfStock defaults to false (out-of-stock items rendered, marked as 0 stock).
refreshRate is 5000ms but is not currently used anywhere; LiveView relies on poll updates, not polling.

openIssues.name: CurrentConfigIsHardcodedNoEnvSelection
openIssues.what: currentConfig = localConfig is a hardcoded source-level binding; switching to networkConfig requires editing this file
openIssues.why: No build-time or runtime mechanism for environment selection. When deploying to a non-localhost target, currentConfig must be edited by hand and the bundle rebuilt. A clean fix would inject the config via a foreign import from a generated JS module, or sniff via window.location.host. Symptom of getting it wrong: API calls go to the wrong host, CORS rejects everything, login fails silently with confusing 'network error' messages.

openIssues.name: HttpsRequiredForLocalhost
openIssues.what: localConfig hardcodes https:// for both apiBaseUrl and appOrigin, which requires a working dev certificate for localhost
openIssues.why: localConfig sets apiBaseUrl and appOrigin to https://localhost URLs. With an untrusted dev certificate the browser drops the Set-Cookie from /auth/login and refuses to send cookies cross-origin, and the console stays silent. Symptom: login returns 2xx, then /auth/me returns 401. Mixing http and https between apiBaseUrl and appOrigin also breaks CORS preflight. The repo's mkcert-style tooling creates the certificate, and a fresh clone has to run it before login works.

currentConfig: Always returns localConfig in the current source. Edit this binding to switch environments.
Other modules import currentConfig and use it for apiBaseUrl and appOrigin (sent as the CORS Origin header).

decisions.name: GqlPostUsesTheSharedRequestCore
decisions.what: gqlPost is API.Request.post to /graphql/inventory with {query}, and returns the data field of the answer
why: Authentication is the session cookie, as for every other request.
A GraphQL error answer has no data field and arrives as Undecodable.

decisions.name: RawGraphqlQueryStringNoSchemaCodegen
decisions.what: Queries and mutations are raw string templates with no codegen or type-safe builder
decisions.why: Yoga.JSON's writeJSON handles serializing MenuItem into the mutation input. No PureScript GraphQL schema codegen exists in this project; a mismatch between the query string and the schema would only surface at runtime. Acceptable because there are only four operations (read/write/update/delete inventory); a larger surface would justify codegen.

openIssues.name: DeleteMutationUsesStringInterpolationForSku
openIssues.what: deleteInventoryGql interpolates sku into the GraphQL query string with manual quoting: deleteMenuItem(sku: \"" <> sku <> "\")
openIssues.why: If sku ever contains a backslash, double-quote, or newline, the mutation breaks (best case) or becomes injection-shaped (worst case). GraphQL parsers do escape-handle string literals, but the client-side interpolation here doesn't escape anything. Currently safe because parseUUID guarantees the input matches [0-9a-f-]+ only, but the guarantee is implicit and easily lost. Fix: use a variables block: { query: 'mutation D($sku: ID!) { deleteMenuItem(sku: $sku) { ... } }', variables: { sku } }.

inventoryQuery: Hardcoded query string requesting every field on every menu item; no field selection or pagination.
Fine because inventories are small; would need rework for thousands of items.

decisions.name: SessionDecidesWhatIsRendered
decisions.what: Every render reads the auth state first: signed out shows the login page whatever the route says; signed in shows the page for the route
why: The session is asked for once at boot (GET /auth/me). Until the answer arrives nothing is rendered; the route matcher only records the route.
After boot the route in the URL is rendered, so a reload on /#/transaction/create returns to the sale page.
Signing in or out renders the current route again. Signing in on the /#/login route goes to /#/ instead.
A session that cannot be read (no cookie, an expired cookie, a response that does not decode, an unknown role) is signed out. No dev user stands in for a real one.

decisions.name: PagesLoadTheirOwnData
decisions.what: main starts no data loads; each page reads what it needs when it is mounted
why: Main used to launch a loader and push its result into a Poll the page subscribed to. A loader that finished before the page subscribed lost its result, because a plain Poll does not replay.
Pages now hold their data in useHot or UI.Remote.useRemote cells, which do replay, and start loading from UI.Remote.onMount.

decisions.name: PagesRegisterCleanupThroughOnLeave
decisions.what: A page that opens a stream or socket hands its close action to onLeave; main runs every registered action before each render
why: Deku has no unmount hook in the version used here.
Without this each visit to the stock room would leave an EventSource open. Browsers allow about six connections per host over HTTP/1.1.

main: authPoll starts as SignedOut. setAuth writes the Ref and pushes the Poll.
The auth push comes before the route push. Route.nav rebuilds on an auth change and its links learn the current route from the route push that follows.
pageFor draws a fresh SKU for the Create route on every render of that route.
The Login route while signed in shows the live view.

openIssues.name: NoRouteGuardByCapability
openIssues.what: A signed-in user who types a URL for a page their role cannot use still gets that page's shell
why: Route.nav hides the link, and the backend refuses the page's requests with 403, which the page shows as text.
Wanted: pageFor checks the same capability Route.navLinks uses and shows a plain refusal.

sseStatus: Renders an SSEStatus poll as a span with a color-coded class and a label.
Pure presentation; consumes only the status poll exposed by Utils.SSE.openSSE.

page: snapshot is a useRemote cell loaded by onMount and by the Refresh button; tabs come from UI.Tabs.tabBar
Takes OnLeave and passes it to the log viewer and the feed monitor.

decisions.name: AdminTabOnly
decisions.what: This module now holds only AdminTab and allTabs; the snapshot state is Types.RemoteData

decisions.name: InMemoryFeedFrameRingBuffer
decisions.what: Feed frames are accumulated in component state up to maxFrames (100); older frames are dropped
decisions.why: Feed traffic can be high-volume; unbounded growth would exhaust browser memory. 100 is large enough to inspect recent activity but small enough to render without slowdown. If durable inspection is needed, the backend's feed history endpoints are the right path.

decisions.name: ConnRefSentinelForRaceCondition
decisions.what: connRef holds Just conn while the WebSocket is intended to be open; the onMessage handler checks this Ref before pushing frames
decisions.why: Without the check, a message that arrives in flight after disconnect would still update component state, causing stale UI. setting connRef to Nothing in onClose / disconnect button breaks the race window. PureScript's WebSocket API doesn't synchronously cancel pending callbacks on close; this Ref-based gate is the manual fix.

feedMonitor: intent: Subscribe to the public inventory feed via WebSocket, render frames as they arrive
WebSocket URL derives from currentConfig.apiBaseUrl by toWsUrl rewriting https:// to wss://.
Frame parsing failures are logged (Console.warn) but not surfaced to the UI.
No automatic reconnect; user must click Connect again if the connection drops.
Each connection's close action is registered with onLeave, so leaving the page closes the socket.
Pressing Connect twice opens two sockets. Both are closed on leave.

decisions.name: LogStreamUsesSSENotWebSocket
decisions.what: Logs stream over SSE (Server-Sent Events) rather than WebSocket
decisions.why: SSE is unidirectional (server -> client) which matches the log streaming use case exactly. SSE has automatic reconnect built in; WebSocket requires manual reconnect logic. SSE works through more proxies and corporate firewalls than WebSocket. Cost: SSE doesn't support binary frames, but logs are text anyway.

logViewer: Opens API.Admin.logStreamUrl through Utils.SSE; the session cookie is the credential.
Entries live in a Ref owned by the connection. Each message is put in front and the list is cut to maxLogEntries (500).
Connect does nothing while a connection is held. Disconnect closes it and clears the list.
The connection's close action is registered with onLeave.
A message that does not decode is logged to the console and skipped.

page: Owns the SKU of the item being created, starting from the one Main passes in.
After a successful create it shows the backend's message above the form and draws a new SKU, which rebuilds the form empty.
A second item created from the same page therefore gets its own SKU.

decisions.name: SalePageNeedsAChosenOpenRegister
decisions.what: load shows the sale screen only when this browser has a chosen register that the backend knows and that is open
why: Nothing here creates or opens a register. When one is missing, gone (404) or closed the page says so and links to /#/register.
The closed-register rule is the front end's. The backend starts a sale on any register id.
With a register in hand, Services.CurrentSale.resume looks for this user's open sale on it.

decisions.name: SaleStartsFromAButton
decisions.what: Opening the sale page starts no sale. With no resumable sale the page shows TxPageNoSale with a Start Sale button, and begin starts the sale when it is pressed
why: load used to call resumeOrStart, so every visit without a resumable sale sent POST /pos/sale. See Services.CurrentSale.NothingHereStartsASaleOnItsOwn.

A button was chosen over starting the sale with the first added item because UI.Transaction.CreateTransaction and its four parts all take a sale that exists. Starting with the first item needs a sale-less state in each of them.
TxPageStatus has six cases: TxPageLoading, TxPageNeedsRegister, TxPageNoSale, TxPageStarting, TxPageReady, TxPageError.
The Start Sale card has the CSS class no-sale and the register message has register-needed; both are styled in the SESSION-ERA PAGES section of app-styles.css.

load: Reads the chosen register id from Services.RegisterService. With none it returns TxPageNeedsRegister without any request.
Fetches the inventory and the register in parallel.
A failed inventory fetch does not stop the page: the status carries Failure 'Inventory unavailable: ...' and the screen can refresh it.
A failed register fetch other than 404 gives TxPageError with the backend's text.
On an open register: a resumable sale gives TxPageReady, none gives TxPageNoSale, and a remembered sale that could not be read gives TxPageError 'Could not load the open sale: ...'.
begin: Calls Services.CurrentSale.startOn. Success gives TxPageReady with the inventory load already fetched; failure gives TxPageError 'Could not start a sale: ...'.
page: Holds the status in a useHot cell and runs load from onMount.
Start Sale sets TxPageStarting before the request, so the button is gone while the request runs and cannot be pressed twice.
Reads the whole inventory when mounted and shows UI.Inventory.DeleteItem.renderDeleteConfirmation for the item whose SKU is in the route.
Uses findItem, itemView and resolveSku from Pages.EditItem.
Reads the whole inventory through API.Inventory.readInventory when mounted and edits the item whose SKU is in the route.
An unknown SKU and a failed fetch both use UI.Inventory.ItemForm.renderError, with different text.
resolveSku: The route segment 'test' stands for testItemUUID. Shared with Pages.DeleteItem.
findItem: Compares the shown form of each item's SKU with the given text.

page: Wrapper around Pages.Admin.Tabs.FeedMonitor.feedMonitor, passing OnLeave through.
Route.navLinks shows the Feed link to every signed-in user.
Reads the inventory through GraphQL.API.Inventory.readInventoryGql when mounted and draws it with UI.Inventory.MenuLiveView.renderInventory.
Takes no arguments. It has no live updates; a reload or a return to the route reads again.
built on UI.Form with loginStyle (hints hidden); Sign In is disabled until both fields are non-blank
username is trimmed, password is sent as typed
On success hands the session the backend returned to onSignedIn. Main decides where to go next.
A refusal shows 'Login failed: ' and the backend's text. A response that does not decode, such as an unknown role, is also an error here and the browser stays signed out.
activity is a useRemote cell loaded by onMount and by the Refresh button; the Override tab is a placeholder
Takes no arguments.

decisions.name: ManagerTabOnly
decisions.what: This module now holds only ManagerTab and allManagerTabs; the activity state is Types.RemoteData

alertBanner: Renders the most-recent new pull request as a dismissable banner with View / X buttons.
onSelect fires the parent's pull-selection handler AND calls onDismiss to clear the banner.
Uses foreign imports showPullNotification and requestNotificationPermission to integrate with the browser Notification API.
If the user denies notification permission, the banner still works; only the OS-level notification is skipped.

messageThread: Renders a scrollable message list with a compose box at the bottom.
Send button is gated on non-empty draft; pressing Send clears the draft on success (whether or not the message actually delivered).
Roles are styled via class names ('role-cashier', 'role-stocker', etc.); presentation only.

actionBtnClass: Maps PullAction to a button-style class (success/danger/warning/primary).
Used for visual distinction of destructive (Cancel) vs constructive (Fulfill) vs ambiguous (Report Issue) actions.
pullCard: Renders a single pull request as a card with status badge, transaction ID, item details, and action buttons.
Action buttons are computed from prStatus via Types.Stock.validActions; an unrecognized status produces zero buttons (see Types.Stock.PullVertexAndStringStatusInParallel).
Messages button is always rendered regardless of status; selecting it opens the MessageThread for this pull.

decisions.name: SSEPushTriggersFullQueueReload
decisions.what: The SSE stream from /stock/queue/stream is used purely as a 'queue changed' notification; the handler ignores the event payload and calls loadQueue to refetch
decisions.why: Avoids encoding the full PullRequest type in the SSE event format; the REST endpoint is the source of truth. Trades extra HTTP requests for simpler protocol and avoids drift between SSE event shape and REST response shape. Cost: one extra round-trip per queue change; acceptable because changes are infrequent (human-initiated).

decisions.name: NewPullDetectionViaPrevQueueDiff
decisions.what: New pull requests are detected by diffing prevQueueRef against the new fetch result rather than from a 'created' event type
decisions.why: The SSE event payload is ignored (see SSEPushTriggersFullQueueReload), so we can't tell from the event whether it was a create or an update. Diffing by prId catches creates without needing event-type discrimination. Side effect: only triggers audio + browser notification + alert banner for new pulls, not for status updates. Edits to existing pulls are silent. If the prev queue is empty (initial load), no notifications fire even if pulls are present; this is intentional to avoid spamming the user on app start.

page: Loads the queue and opens the stream from UI.Remote.onMount.
The stream is API.Stock.queueStreamUrl with the session cookie as the credential. Its close action is registered with onLeave.
Request errors are shown in the status bar with the backend's text.
useRef: unsafePerformEffect-based Ref creation; safe because Ref.new is idempotent and the Ref is captured in the continuation's closure.
Workaround for not having a useRef hook in Deku; revisit if Deku adds one.

openIssues.name: StreamAuthNotConfirmedInABrowser
openIssues.what: The queue stream relies on the backend's CORS answer allowing credentials for an EventSource; this has been checked only against a mock
why: Utils.SSE opens the EventSource with withCredentials. The backend's reflectOriginMiddleware adds Access-Control-Allow-Origin and Allow-Credentials to every response, read from source.
If the stream badge stays on Reconnecting against the real backend, look here first.

decisions.name: VoidAndRefundFollowTheBackendRules
decisions.what: Void is offered with capCanVoidTransaction on a sale UI.Transaction.Model.voidable accepts; refund with capCanRefundTransaction on a sale refundable accepts
why: A refunded sale shows as Refunded and offers neither. A cashier sees no action at all.
Both need a reason, which is posted as a JSON string.
The backend decides. A refusal shows the backend's text, and the list is read again after every attempt, so a sale changed on another screen shows its real status.
Whether a void or a refund puts stock back is backend configuration. The page does not say either way.

page: Lists every sale from API.Sale.getAllSales, newest first, with time (UTC), status, line count, total and id.
One request runs at a time; buttons are disabled while busy and until a reason is typed.
Uses formatStatus and statusClass from UI.Transaction.CreateTransaction.

openIssues.name: HistoryShowsNoLinesOrRefundRows
openIssues.what: A row shows a line count and a total only; the lines, the payments and the refund row of a refunded sale are not shown
why: API.Refund.getAllRefunds and getRefund have no caller.
The new CSS classes sale-row, sale-created, sale-lines, sale-total, sale-id, sale-actions, sale-list and sale-history have no rules yet.

decisions.name: NavLinksAreShownByCapability
decisions.what: navLinks pairs each link with the capability check the backend applies to that area; visibleLinks filters by the session's capabilities
why: A signed-out browser sees only Login. A signed-in one sees its links, its user name and Logout.

The checks: inventory view, create item, process transaction (New Transaction and Sales), open or manage registers, admin dashboard, view reports (Manager), fulfill orders (Stock Room). Feed is shown to everyone signed in.
This decides what is shown. The backend decides every request.

nav: Rebuilds on every auth change. Logout calls the signOut action Main passes in.
route: RouteDuplex' definition: bidirectional parser/printer between Route and URL hash strings.
Registers is /#/register. Edit and Delete take a (string segment) parameter; Pages.EditItem.resolveSku special-cases the slug 'test'.
visibleLinks: Pure, and covered by test/Auth.purs for each role.

decisions.name: AuthStateHoldsTheBackendSession
decisions.what: AuthState is SignedIn SessionResponse or SignedOut; the user id, role and capabilities are the ones the backend sent
why: It used to hold a dev user chosen by role, with capabilities derived from the role on the client. An unknown role became the admin dev user.
The session itself is an HttpOnly cookie. This value decides only what the screens show.

capabilities: The session's own capabilities when signed in, Types.Auth.emptyCapabilities when signed out.
can: Reads one capability; false for every capability when signed out.
session: Just the session when signed in.
isSignedIn: True for SignedIn, false for SignedOut.

decisions.name: RegisterIdInLocalStorage
decisions.what: The id of the register this browser sells on is kept in localStorage under the key 'register_id'
why: A till is identified by the device, not by who is signed in.
The id is written only by chooseRegister, from the 'Use on this device' button on Pages.Registers. Nothing generates one.
The key is the one the app has always used, so a browser that already had a register keeps it.

chosenRegisterId: Nothing when the key is absent or does not parse as a UUID.
Does not check that the register is known to the backend; Pages.CreateTransaction.load does.
newRegister: Builds a closed register with a fresh id and zero drawer amounts for API.Register.createRegister. Makes no request.

decisions.name: AdminActionAsTaggedSumWithPositionalContents
decisions.what: AdminAction is a sum type (RevokeSession, ForceCloseRegister, ClearRateLimitForIp, SetLowStockThreshold, TriggerSnapshotExport); WriteForeign emits {tag, contents} with constructor-shape-dependent contents
decisions.why: {tag, contents} matches the backend's expected JSON shape; the tag is the constructor name, contents is the argument(s). ForceCloseRegister has TWO args (uuid, reason) and serializes as a positional array [uuidString, reason]; the backend expects positional args here, not a named object. Adding a third arg to ForceCloseRegister means coordinating with the backend's positional decoder. TriggerSnapshotExport has no args; serializes as just {tag: 'TriggerSnapshotExport'}.

decisions.name: AdminSnapshotIsPointInTimeServerState
decisions.what: AdminSnapshot is a wide record bundling uptime, sessions, registers, inventory summary, DB pool stats, broadcaster queue depths
decisions.why: Rendered as the dashboard Overview tab; designed to fit on one screen as a grid of stat cards. Adding a field requires backend coordination since the wire shape is shared. Snapshot is fetched on demand (mount and refresh button); there's no streaming snapshot - bcAvailabilitySeq is the closest thing to a freshness watermark.

decisions.name: FourRoleHierarchyWithMonotonicCapabilities
decisions.what: UserRole has a strict ordering Customer < Cashier < Manager < Admin; each higher role's capabilities are a strict superset of the next-lower role's
decisions.why: Models the typical retail hierarchy where higher roles can do everything lower roles can plus more. Allows whenRoleAtLeast in UI.Components.AuthGuard to gate features by minimum role. Capabilities are explicit per-role rather than computed from the ordering, so the table-of-truth is searchable in source. Adding a new capability requires touching all four *Capabilities records, which forces an explicit choice about which roles get it.

capabilitiesForRole: Total function over UserRole; no Maybe or Either needed.
Each branch returns the corresponding *Capabilities top-level value, not a fresh record. Modifying *Capabilities propagates.
emptyCapabilities: All boolean fields are false; Services.AuthService.capabilities returns it for a signed-out browser.
Also the base for the *Capabilities records via record update syntax.

openIssues.name: CapabilityTableIsAClientCopy
openIssues.what: capabilitiesForRole and the four per-role records are a hand-kept copy of the backend's capability table, and the app no longer reads them
why: The app takes capabilities from the session the backend sends. Only the tests use this table, to build sessions per role.
No fixture ties the copy to the backend table.

decisions.name: FeedFrameWireShapeUsesFullStateNotDeltas
decisions.what: FeedFrame is { seq, payload, timestamp } where payload is the entire AvailableItem; each frame is the full current state of one item, not a delta
decisions.why: Simplifies the consumer: no need to apply a diff against prior state; latest frame wins. seq is a monotonically-increasing per-location sequence number that clients can use to detect gaps. Cost: bandwidth-per-change is the full item record vs a tiny delta. Acceptable for retail-scale item counts; would not scale to high-frequency-trading-style updates. If gap detection becomes important, the consumer needs to re-fetch the snapshot endpoint after a seq jump.

decisions.name: NoFormValidationHere
decisions.what: validateMenuItem and the string form-input types were removed; parsing form text is UI.Form.Parser's job and MenuItem is built directly by UI.Inventory.ItemForm.menuItemForm
why: Types.Formatting and Utils.Validation were deleted with them.

findItemNameBySku: Returns 'Unknown Item' (literal string) for SKUs not in inventory; never Nothing.
Used in transaction display where missing items are valid (the underlying menu item may have been deleted after the transaction).
findItemBySku: Linear scan; O(n). Acceptable because inventories are small (hundreds, not millions).
Returns Nothing if no match; consumers typically display 'Unknown Item' or treat as a delete.
generateClassName: Concatenates species/category/subcategory into a CSS class string with toClassName-normalized parts.
Used for visual differentiation in the menu live view; CSS rules elsewhere assume specific class names.
compareMenuItems: Multi-field comparison driven by LiveViewConfig.sortFields; first non-EQ result wins.
Each field can be Ascending or Descending; Descending inverts via invertOrdering.
EQ on all fields means the items are considered equal for ordering purposes; sortBy is not stable in PureScript so equal elements may swap on resort.

parseLocationId: Reverses locationIdToString via parseUUID; returns Nothing on invalid UUID format.
LocationId itself is a newtype wrapper around UUID; exists purely to prevent accidental mixing of LocationId with other UUID-typed fields (RegisterId, EmployeeId, etc).
Show, ReadForeign, WriteForeign on LocationId all delegate to the underlying UUID, so wire format is indistinguishable from a bare UUID.

decisions.name: ManagerAlertIsTheTaggedSumTheBackendWrites
decisions.what: ManagerAlert is a sum type decoded from {tag, contents}, the shape Aeson's generic instance writes for the backend type
why: LowInventoryAlert: sku, item name, quantity on hand, threshold. StaleTransactionAlert: sale id, seconds open. RegisterVarianceAlert: register id, expected minus counted in cents.
The front end used to expect a flat record with a tag and optional fields. The backend never wrote that shape, so every alert lost its details, and the old tests pinned the wrong shape.
Decoding is strict: an unknown tag or a contents array of the wrong length fails the whole response.
test/Wire.purs holds a backend-shaped activity summary with all three alerts.

openIssues.name: DayStatsMeaningNotAgreedWithOwner
openIssues.what: LocationDayStats is displayed without saying what the numbers mean; the backend definitions changed when REFUNDED was added
why: Backend Server.Manager.buildDayStats: ldsTxCount counts sales whose status is Completed or Refunded; ldsRevenue is net of returns; ldsRefundCount counts sales of the day flagged refunded; ldsAvgTxValue is net revenue divided by the sale count.
The average formula was chosen by the implementer and has not been confirmed by the owner.
'Today' is the UTC day.

decisions.name: SaleMoneyNonNegativeRefundMoneyNonPositive
decisions.what: SaleMoney is a smart-constructor newtype requiring cents >= 0; RefundMoney requires cents <= 0
decisions.why: Sign convention is enforced at the type level so a refund value cannot accidentally appear in a sale record (and vice versa). negateToRefund / negateFromRefund are the explicit conversion functions when crossing between sale and refund contexts. mkSaleMoney / mkRefundMoney return Maybe; unsafeMkSaleMoney / unsafeMkRefundMoney skip validation (used in pure-computation paths where the sign is structurally guaranteed). ReadForeign uses the safe constructor and fails parsing with a clear error if the sign is wrong; never silently truncates.

negateToRefund: Converts SaleMoney -> RefundMoney by negating the cents.
If applied to SaleMoney 0, returns RefundMoney 0 (which is valid in both sign domains).
unsafeMkSaleMoney: Skips the >= 0 check; caller must guarantee non-negativity.
No longer used by the app; only the tests call it.
subtractSale: Returns Maybe SaleMoney; subtracting a larger amount yields Nothing (would violate the non-negative invariant).
Use case: discount application can't reduce a price below zero.

decisions.name: RefundQuantityIsNotNegated
decisions.what: SaleQuantity and RefundQuantity both require a count of zero or more; only refund money is negative
why: The backend writes a refund line's quantity as the number of units returned. Its toRefundQuantity does not negate.
The front end used to require zero or less, so a refund with lines did not decode.
toRefundQuantity and toSaleQuantity keep the count as it is.

subtractSaleQuantity: Returns Maybe SaleQuantity; subtracting more than available yields Nothing.
Use case: removing items from a cart line cannot reduce qty below zero.
oneSaleQuantity: Defined as SaleQuantity 1 for ergonomic comparison; the most common single-unit cart addition value.

decisions.name: RegisterWireShapeMirrorsHaskellRecord
decisions.what: Register is a plain record matching the Haskell backend's Register record field-for-field
why: registerIsOpen decides which controls Pages.Registers shows; the backend refuses to open an open register or close a closed one (409).
The Maybe fields are Nothing for a register that was never opened. Yoga.JSON leaves a Nothing field out when writing, and the backend accepts that.
The variance at close is expected minus counted and is computed by the backend.

decisions.name: RegisterRequestsNameNoEmployee
decisions.what: OpenRegisterRequest holds only the starting cash and CloseRegisterRequest only the counted cash, both in cents
why: The backend takes the acting user from the session. The employee id fields left the wire format on both sides on 2026-10-10.

openIssues.name: CartTotalsHasNoUser
openIssues.what: CartTotals and EntityId are no longer used by the app
why: Their users, Services.TransactionService and Services.Cart, were deleted. Safe to delete after a search of the tests.

decisions.name: SessionResponseCarriesBackendCapabilities
decisions.what: SessionResponse (returned by /auth/me and /auth/login) includes sessionCapabilities, the backend's authoritative view of what the user can do
why: Services.AuthService holds the whole SessionResponse and every capability check in the app reads sessionCapabilities.
The backend can change what a role may do and the screens follow without a front end change.

decisions.name: PullVertexAndStringStatusInParallel
decisions.what: PullVertex is a typed enum but PullRequest.prStatus is a String, and validActions/statusClass dispatch on the String not the enum
decisions.why: The backend serializes pull request status as a string in the JSON wire format; PullVertex exists for typed code paths but the wire model is the source of truth. validActions and statusClass take String specifically because they are called on prStatus values fresh off the wire with no enum conversion step. Cost: a typo in a status string silently produces an empty action list (no buttons render) rather than a compile error. Mitigation would be a parsePullVertex :: String -> Maybe PullVertex used at the API boundary.

actionLabel: Maps PullAction to the human-readable button label.
Total over PullAction; adding a constructor requires updating this function.
statusClass: Maps prStatus string to a CSS class name; used for visual differentiation of pull cards.
Unrecognized status returns empty string (no class applied).
validActions: Returns the list of PullActions the UI should offer for a given prStatus string.
Pattern matches on the EXACT string forms: 'PullPending', 'PullAccepted', 'PullPulling', 'PullIssue'. Other strings (including PullFulfilled and PullCancelled) return [].
Terminal states (Fulfilled, Cancelled) have no valid actions; the UI renders no action buttons for them.
ActionRetry on PullIssue is intended to transition back to PullPulling (reattempt the pull) per the topology, but this is enforced server-side; the action label is just 'Retry'.

decisions.name: RefundMoneyNegativeRefundQuantityNot
decisions.what: Refund amounts are RefundMoney (zero or negative cents); refund line quantities are RefundQuantity (zero or more)
why: The backend negates every money field of the sale and keeps each line's quantity and unit price as they were.
itemPricePerUnit is SaleMoney for that reason.
test/Wire.purs decodes a backend-shaped refund.

decisions.name: SaleSpecificMoneyAndQuantityTypes
decisions.what: Sale.Item uses SaleMoney and SaleQuantity rather than raw Discrete USD / Int; payments and totals likewise use SaleMoney
decisions.why: SaleMoney is a smart-constructor newtype that requires non-negative cents; refunds use the inverted RefundMoney type. Compile-time prevents accidentally placing refund amounts into a sale record or vice versa. All field-level money/qty types in Sale.* are SaleMoney/SaleQuantity; converting to refund is an explicit operation via Types.Primitives.Money.negateToRefund. See Types.Primitives.Money and Types.Primitives.Quantity for the smart constructor invariants. Alongside the money types, SaleType is an enum of StandardSale/Exchange/InventoryAdjustment/ManagerComp/Administrative (serialized as PascalCase via WriteForeign). It distinguishes the business purpose of a sale transaction: StandardSale drives the normal POS flow, the others are special-purpose. The backend sets the kind; every sale it starts is a StandardSale.

decisions.name: DualCaseFormatForReadForeignInstances
decisions.what: ReadForeign instances accept BOTH PascalCase and SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE; WriteForeign emits only PascalCase; Show emits SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE
decisions.why: The backend's wire format historically used SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE; a migration to PascalCase happened (or is happening) and both forms exist in storage and on the wire. Accepting both forms in ReadForeign means the frontend doesn't break against either old or new backend builds. WriteForeign emits only the new PascalCase format; the SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE branch is purely for reading legacy data. Show is INCONSISTENT with WriteForeign: showTransactionStatus emits 'CREATED' / 'IN_PROGRESS' for log readability, while writeForeignTransactionStatus emits 'Created' / 'InProgress' for the wire. Two output formats per type, deliberately, because logs and wire have different conventions. PaymentMethod has a special case: the 'Other s' constructor serializes as 'Other:s' (colon-prefixed); the readForeign side strips the prefix and falls back to Other <whole-string> on no match (never fails parsing). Applies to all readForeign*/writeForeign*/show* instances for TransactionStatus, PaymentMethod, TaxCategory, TransactionType, LedgerEntryType, AccountType. When the backend migration completes and no SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE values remain in the wild, the legacy ReadForeign branches can be deleted. Affects is empty here because chase's drift checker validates invariant attachment against signatures only; instance dictionary names live in chaseDataDecls which is not drift-checked.

decisions.name: DiscreteMoneyUSDForAllAmounts
decisions.what: All Transaction, TransactionItem, PaymentTransaction, LedgerEntry money fields use DiscreteMoney USD
decisions.why: DiscreteMoney is a phantom-currency-tagged Discrete (Int cents) wrapper from purescript-money. Prevents accidental mixing of currencies and accidental Number arithmetic. Wire format serializes as a plain Int (cents); the WriteForeign instance unwraps to Int.

maybeToNullable: Wrapper around Data.Nullable.toNullable; named for use-site clarity in the WriteForeign instances that need to emit JSON null for Nothing fields.
Used pervasively in writeForeignTransaction and writeForeignPaymentTransaction to convert Maybe fields to Nullable before serialization.

openIssues.name: StatusParsingIsLenient
openIssues.what: The ReadForeign instances accept more than one spelling per constructor (for example both "Refunded" and "REFUNDED"), while WriteForeign writes "Refunded" and Show gives "REFUNDED"
why: A lenient reader hides drift between the two code bases. The backend parsers are lenient in the same way.
Wanted: one spelling per value on the wire, pinned by golden JSON fixtures shared by the Haskell and PureScript suites. Those fixtures do not exist yet.

decisions.name: ManualUUIDv4ImplementationNotCryptoRandomUUID
decisions.what: genUUID is a manual UUIDv4 builder using Effect.Random.random, NOT crypto.randomUUID or any cryptographically secure source
decisions.why: Effect.Random.random is Math.random under the hood; not suitable for cryptographic purposes. For inventory item UUIDs, transaction UUIDs, and similar non-secret identifiers, this is fine. A safer implementation would foreign import crypto.randomUUID() from the browser's WebCrypto API (available in all modern browsers since ~2022). Switching is a one-line foreign import; the only reason it hasn't happened is nobody has needed cryptographic UUIDs yet.

openIssues.name: GenUUIDNotCryptographicallySecure
openIssues.what: genUUID's randomness comes from Math.random; an attacker observing some UUIDs could in principle predict subsequent ones
openIssues.why: PRNG predictability matters if UUIDs are ever used as authorization tokens, password reset links, or share-link nonces. Currently genUUID is used for transaction IDs, item IDs, payment IDs, register IDs - all server-validated, so predictability is not currently a vulnerability vector. Becomes a problem the moment a future feature uses a UUID as a capability token.
blocking: any future use of genUUID for security-sensitive identifiers

genUUID: Sets version 4 (random) by ORing 0x4000 into the time_hi field.
Sets variant 10xx by ORing 0x8000 into clock_seq.
Output format matches parseUUID's expected pattern (lowercase hex, hyphens at standard positions).
validateUUID: Trims input before parsing; returns V (Array String) UUID with field-name-prefixed error.
Used by Types.Inventory.validateMenuItem and similar form validators.
parseUUID: Strict regex match: 8-4-4-4-12 lowercase hex with hyphens. Uppercase hex is rejected (would need a flag change).
Returns Nothing on any deviation from the canonical form; the regex doesn't validate version/variant bits.
Used by ReadForeign instance and form validators.

decisions.name: WhenCapableUsesGuardForReactiveGating
decisions.what: whenCapable wraps children in Deku.Hooks.guard so the children are only mounted (not just hidden) when the capability is true
decisions.why: guard fully unmounts vs hides; this avoids hidden but mounted children running event handlers or holding refs. Means capability changes during a session (e.g. role downgrade) immediately remove the gated UI. Cost: re-mounting on cap toggle drops any component-local state. For most caps this is fine because they don't toggle mid-session.

openIssues.name: DisabledUnlessIsNoOp
openIssues.what: disabledUnless ignores both arguments and returns children unchanged
openIssues.why: Probably intended to add a 'disabled' attribute to children based on capability, but the implementation is a passthrough. Currently no callers, so this hasn't caused visible problems, but the name lies about what it does. Either implement properly (would need to know how to attribute-mutate Nuts) or delete the function.

openIssues.name: ModuleHasNoUser
openIssues.what: Nothing in the app imports this module
why: Route.nav and the pages read capabilities from the session record directly.
Keep it only if reactive gating inside a page is wanted later.

whenRoleAtLeast: Compares the user's role to a minimum via the Ord instance; relies on Types.Auth.FourRoleHierarchyWithMonotonicCapabilities.
Cleanest gate for 'manager or higher' checks; the per-capability gates are more granular but require knowing the right cap name.

deleteItem: Two-state UI: confirmation prompt -> success or error message after submit.
On success, displays a 'Return to Inventory' link; the user must click it (no auto-redirect).
Submit button is disabled while submitting to prevent double-clicks.
An error shows the backend's text; an unknown SKU is 'Item not found'.

decisions.name: ItemFormOnUIForm
decisions.what: menuItemForm is one applicative Form MenuItem built from four section sub-forms; itemForm runs it and owns only the status message and submitting flag
why: Replaced a 650-line version with two useHot cells per field and about twelve touch points per field.
CreateMode carries the SKU and an onCreated callback; EditMode carries the item.

openIssues.name: StrictNameRuleBlocksExistingItems
openIssues.what: Name, brand, subcategory, strain, creator and dominant terpene use required >=> alphanumeric; edit mode parses the stored value, so an existing item with an apostrophe, period or ampersand shows a hint and cannot be saved until changed
why: Owner's decision 2026-10-04: keep the strict rule for now. extendedAlphanumeric >=> maxLen 50 is the one-line alternative in requiredName.

menuItemForm: price field uses Parser.cents and wraps in Discrete; category and species use the enum select
initial text comes from the item in EditMode and is blank in CreateMode
itemForm: submit button is styled disabled while invalid and the click handler ignores invalid results

On a successful create it calls the mode's onCreated with the backend's message; Pages.CreateItem then supplies a new SKU and the form is rebuilt. On a successful edit it shows the message and keeps the form.

renderInventory: Filters out-of-stock items if config.hideOutOfStock is true; then sorts via Types.Inventory.compareMenuItems.
Empty inventory shows an 'empty-inventory' message; otherwise renders a grid via renderItem.
Stats footer shows total item count BEFORE filtering.
renderItem: Renders one MenuItem as a card with image, brand, name, category, species, strain, price, description, quantity, and edit/delete action links.
Description is summarized via Utils.Formatting.summarizeLongText (100-char limit with ellipsis).
Action links are <a> tags using URL hashes (/#/edit/<sku>, /#/delete/<sku>); no JS handler, the router catches the hash change.

openIssues.name: EditAndDeleteLinksShownToEveryone
openIssues.what: renderItem draws Edit and Delete links on every card whatever the user's capabilities are
why: A user without capCanEditItem or capCanDeleteItem reaches the form and the backend refuses the save with 403.
renderInventory would need the session's capabilities passed in.

decisions.name: OneSaleScreenPerSale
decisions.what: createTransaction holds which sale is on screen; saleScreen is rebuilt from scratch when New Sale swaps it, so filters, the payment form and the message start clean
why: saleScreen owns four cells: the sale, the inventory (useRemote), the Activity, and the status message.
All actions go through perform, which sets the Activity, runs the request, replaces the sale, and refreshes the inventory.

saleScreen: the payment form is run here (runFormWith paymentStyle paymentForm) and passed to paymentPanel so the screen can list its errors
the status panel shows two lists: payment form errors and Model.finalizeBlockers; it reuses the inventory-errors-* CSS classes
A refused action shows 'Error: ' and the backend's text. After a 409 or a 404 (saleIsStale) the sale is read again with API.Sale.getSale.
New Sale calls Services.CurrentSale.startNext with the finished sale
inventory is refreshed on mount and after every action, accepted or refused
saleIsStale: True for Refused 409 and Refused 404. A 400 and a 403 leave the sale on screen as it is.

openIssues.name: InventoryOnlyRefreshedAfterOwnActions
openIssues.what: saleScreen refreshes inventory on mount and after each of its own actions; it does not hear about sales, voids or refunds made on other registers
why: The server is the source of truth and refuses an add with 400 insufficient inventory, so the result is a refused click on a row that looked available, not a wrong sale.

A void or refund may or may not put stock back depending on server configuration; the screen has no signal for that either. Whether the backend relay publishes those changes was deduced, not verified.
Wanted: the sale screen subscribes to live inventory the way the live menu view does.

playSound: Creates a fresh <audio> element on every call; the element is not added to the DOM and is garbage-collected after the play completes.
Sound paths are hardcoded under /assets/sounds/; the web server must serve them.
Browser autoplay policies may silently block playback if no user gesture has occurred; this is a browser-level behavior, not handled here.

summarizeLongText: Replaces newlines with spaces, collapses runs of whitespace, truncates to 100 chars with '...' suffix.
Uses unsafePartial on the regex compile; the regex is a string literal so the partial is safe.
formatDollarAmount: Round-trips a string through Number.fromString; non-numeric input passes through unchanged.
Pads to exactly 2 decimals; truncates beyond 2 (does NOT round).
parseCommaList: Splits on comma, trims each, drops empty.
Empty input returns []; this is the inverse of joining with ', '.
getAllEnumValues: Returns all values of a BoundedEnum via catMaybes (toEnum <$> range 0 (fromEnum top)).
formatCentsToDollars: Integer arithmetic only. Always two decimal places.
A negative amount keeps its sign: -250 gives '-2.50' and -5 gives '-0.05'.
formatDateTime: Writes a DateTime as 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM UTC' with padded fields. Times from the backend are UTC.

formatDiscretePrice: Uses numeric (no currency symbol) format from purescript-money.
Consumers in the UI typically prepend '$' as a separate text node.
fromDollars: Floors (dollars * 100); inputs with more than 2 decimal places lose the third decimal.
Matches the convention in Types.Inventory.validateMenuItem for consistency.
parseMoneyString: Trims input then calls Number.fromString; non-numeric input returns Nothing.
Does NOT handle currency symbols, commas, or whitespace within the number; caller is responsible for normalization.

decisions.name: SSEStatusViaForeignImportPushedIntoPoll
decisions.what: openSSEImpl is a foreign import that takes both an onMessage and an onStatus callback; the PureScript wrapper translates status strings into SSEStatus and pushes them into a Poll
decisions.why: EventSource lifecycle events (open, error, close, reconnecting) need to be exposed to the UI for the SSEStatus indicator widget. A Poll lets multiple consumers subscribe to status changes (the SSEStatus component, plus potentially logging or analytics). Mapping status strings in the foreign import boundary keeps the JS side simple (it just stringifies); typed mapping happens on the PS side.

decisions.name: EventSourceIsOpenedWithCredentials
decisions.what: The foreign openSSEImpl creates the EventSource with withCredentials: true
why: The streams are on the API origin and authenticate with the session cookie. A cross-origin EventSource sends cookies only with this option.
Stream URLs used to carry the user id as a query parameter, which the backend never read.

openSSE: intent: Open an EventSource, return a connection object with a status Poll and a close action
Status starts as SSEConnecting (via the pure SSEConnecting <|> statusRef.poll combinator).
Unknown status strings from the JS layer fall through to SSEConnecting; this is permissive by design so future JS-side status types don't break the type checker.

openWebSocket: Foreign import _openWebSocket takes individual callbacks (onMessage, onOpen, onClose, onError); the PS wrapper bundles them as WSCallbacks for ergonomics.
WSConnection is opaque (foreign import data); the only operation is closeWebSocket.
No automatic reconnect; consumers must observe onClose / onError and reopen if desired.
toWsUrl: Rewrites https:// -> wss:// and http:// -> ws://; otherwise passes through unchanged.
Used to derive WS endpoints from the same currentConfig.apiBaseUrl that REST uses, so dev/prod switches automatically.

decisions.name: ParseDontValidateAtTheInputBoundary
decisions.what: A field parser is String -> Either String a; it returns the typed value or the hint text. There is no separate Boolean validity rule and no second parse at submit.
why: The old kit had a ValidationRule (String -> Boolean), a separate error string, and validateMenuItem re-parsing at submit; the three could disagree.
String-returning parsers chain with >=>.

cents: digit arithmetic only: "19.99" -> 1999. The old path floored a float and produced 1998.
rejects more than two decimals, negatives, blanks, and amounts above 21474835.99 (Int overflow guard)
percentage: requires the trailing % and returns the string unchanged, because StrainLineage stores thc/cbg as text with the sign
commaList: splits on ",", trims each entry and filters out ""; always Right, so "a,, ,b" gives ["a","b"] and "" gives []
optional: blank input is Right Nothing; anything else must satisfy the inner parser

decisions.name: ApplicativeFormOverDekuHooks
decisions.what: Form a is a newtype over Style -> (Built a -> Nut) -> Nut with Functor/Apply/Applicative only; each field owns one useHot cell of raw text and validity is the parser mapped over it
why: Adding a form field is one line in an ado block plus one name in the result record.
Applicative only: the set of fields is static, so reset and error accumulation (V (Array String)) are derivable. There is deliberately no Monad instance.
Validity is never stored, so it cannot go stale.

decisions.name: StyleSuppliedAtRunSite
decisions.what: All CSS classes come from a Style record passed to runFormWith; field definitions carry no presentation
why: ItemForm uses defaultStyle (Tailwind), Login and the payment form pass their own.
Setting hint = "hidden" hides hints for forms that report problems elsewhere.

decisions.name: DependentFieldsStayMounted
decisions.what: dependent passes the first form's parsed value as a Poll to a second form built once; visibleWhen hides a sub-form with the 'hidden' class and makes it yield Nothing
why: Hidden fields keep their text and do not count against validity.
Fields cannot be created dynamically (for example one input per cart line); that needs a different combinator.

select: option values are BoundedEnum indices, not Show strings; the prompt option has value "" and parses to Left
choice: button group over an explicit list for types that are not BoundedEnum (PaymentMethod has Other String); always valid; ignores Style and takes its classes from the spec
textArea: Deku's textarea row has no value attribute, so the binding uses attributeAtYourOwnRisk "value"
readOnly: allocates no useHot cell: result is pure (toV label (parse value)) and reset is pure unit
renders a disabled input with " bg-gray-100" appended to Style.input; ItemForm uses it for the SKU with Parser.uuid
isValid: maps Data.Validation.Semigroup.isValid over Built.result; ItemForm and Login use it to style and disable their submit buttons
a sub-form hidden by visibleWhen yields Nothing and never makes it false
inputField: stores untrimmed text; parsers trim. Trimming on every keystroke would eat the space while typing a multi-word value.

decisions.name: OneRemoteDataType
decisions.what: RemoteData a = NotAsked | Loading | Failure String | Success a replaces the per-page SnapshotStatus, ActivityStatus and ReportStatus ADTs
why: Failure carries text. UI.Remote.useRemote fills it with API.Request.describe of the error.
Pages.CreateTransaction keeps its own status type because it has extra cases. fromEither has no caller now.

useRemote: Takes an Aff (Either ApiError a) and holds RemoteData a in a useHot cell.
reload sets Loading and then fetches; refresh fetches and keeps the current value on screen until the answer arrives.
A Left becomes Failure with API.Request.describe of the error.
onMount: uses Deku.DOM.Self.self_. DL.load_ on a div or span never fires because browsers do not raise load on those elements.
The effect can run before the element's children subscribe, so state it sets must be in a useHot cell, which replays.
viewRemote: one <#~> over the RemoteData Poll; RemoteView says how to draw NotAsked, Loading and Failure

tabBar: one D.button per tab labelled with show; the selected one gets " active" appended to TabStyle.tab and a click calls the select callback
the transaction screen's category tabs are divs keyed by Maybe ItemCategory and deliberately do not use this

reportsPanel: the report is a useRemote cell starting NotAsked; it is fetched only when Generate Report is pressed
The request carries the current time and Config.Entity.dummyLocationId, because the backend decodes both fields.

openIssues.name: DailyReportFiguresAreNotReal
openIssues.what: reportsPanel shows dailyReportCash, dailyReportCard and dailyReportOther as if they were takings by payment method; the backend does not compute them from payments
why: The cash and card split is invented server-side; only the total and the transaction count come from sales.
The backend reads neither the date nor the location in the request.
The backend day rolls over at UTC midnight, not at the shop's local midnight.
blocking: using the daily report for cash-up

decisions.name: SaleIsNeverEditedLocally
decisions.what: The pure functions here only read the sale the backend returned; the screen has no local cart, no local totals and no tax arithmetic
why: Every action returns the whole SaleTransaction from the backend and the screen replaces its copy.
Functions take open record rows so tests can pass small records.

decisions.name: RefundedIsAClosedStatus
decisions.what: isOpen is false for Refunded, and finalizeBlockers reports 'Transaction has been refunded'
why: Matches the backend: a refunded sale keeps its row with status REFUNDED, accepts no further writes, and cannot be voided.

availableToAdd: returns the item's quantity as reported. The backend inventory endpoints already subtract every open reservation, including this cart's, so nothing is subtracted here.
addBlocker: checks in order: requested <= 0 gives "Quantity must be greater than 0"; availableToAdd <= 0 gives "Out of stock"; requested > available gives "Only N available"
client-side hint only: backend DB.Transaction.addTransactionItem makes the real decision and answers 400 on InsufficientInventory
finalizeBlockers: must agree with the backend's Domain.SaleRules.finalizeProblems; an empty array enables Process Payment
quantityInCart: sums across lines with the same SKU
isBusy: any Activity other than Idle; every button on the screen is disabled while busy
canResume: True when the sale is open, was opened by the given user and is on the given register. Used by Services.CurrentSale.
voidable: True for Created, InProgress and Completed. Mirrors the backend, which refuses to void a voided or refunded sale.
refundable: True for Completed only. Mirrors the backend.

openIssues.name: FinalizeBlockersNotTiedToBackendRules
openIssues.what: finalizeBlockers is a hand-kept copy of backend Domain.SaleRules.finalizeProblems; no shared fixture or test makes the two agree
why: The backend is the authority and refuses finalize with 409 and its own reasons. If the two lists differ, the button is enabled and the request is refused, or the button is disabled for a sale the backend would accept.
Wanted: golden JSON cases (sale in, reasons out) checked by both the Haskell and the PureScript suites.

openIssues.name: OverpaymentIsInvisible
openIssues.what: remainingCents clamps at 0, so a sale whose payments exceed the total looks the same as one paid exactly
why: The backend does not record or refuse an overpayment either; what should happen (refuse, or record change due) is an undecided sale rule.

openIssues.name: VoidAndRefundRulesAreAClientCopy
openIssues.what: voidable and refundable are hand-kept copies of the backend's void and refund rules
why: The backend decides and answers 409; a wrong copy shows a button whose request is refused, or hides one that would work.
They belong in the same golden fixtures as finalizeBlockers.

inventoryPicker: the table is rebuilt only when the inventory or a filter changes; per-row cart count and button state follow Polls
category filter is Maybe ItemCategory compared by Eq, not by Show string

cartView: item names are looked up in the inventory; with no inventory, lines show the 'Unknown Item' fallback
totals are the sale's stored saleSubtotal / saleTaxTotal / saleTotal

openIssues.name: NoQuantityControlOnALine
openIssues.what: cartView offers only remove for a line; changing a quantity means removing the line and adding it again
why: See API.SaleCommand.NoSetQuantityCommand.

paymentForm: method is a choice button group; Tendered is visible only for Cash and Auth Code only for Credit; a hidden field yields Nothing
amount uses Parser.cents; tendered is optional cents
paymentPanel: Add Payment is disabled while busy, while the form is invalid, or when the sale is not open

actionBar: Process Payment is hidden and New Sale shown once the sale is not open
Clear Items is enabled only for an open sale with items

addItem: Sends the sale id, the SKU and the quantity. The backend prices the line.

decisions.name: ServerIsTheOnlyPricer
decisions.what: Every action sends ids and quantities only and replaces the sale on screen with the SaleTransaction the backend returns
why: The backend decides each sale write under a row lock on the sale and may refuse it; the front end never computes a price, tax, change or stock level that is then trusted.

decisions.name: MirrorsBackendRequestTypes
decisions.what: Request record field names match backend Types.Transaction.Request exactly; every command returns Sale.SaleTransaction
why: Routes are under /pos/sale and are served by backend Server.SaleCommand.
StartSaleRequest names a register and a location and no employee. The backend records the session user as the opener.

Every command returns Either ApiError. The refusals are: 400 insufficient inventory or a line the pricing rules reject, 403 the sale belongs to another employee, 404 not found, 409 the sale is no longer open or finalize was refused.

openIssues.name: NoIdempotencyKeyOnWrites
openIssues.what: addItem and addPayment carry no client-generated request id; a retry after a lost response adds a second line or a second payment
why: The backend has no idempotency handling either; this is an open backend item and needs a field on both request types.
blocking: safe retry of add item and add payment

openIssues.name: NoSetQuantityCommand
openIssues.what: There is no command to change the quantity of a line; the only way is removeItem followed by addItem
why: Between the two calls the stock is back on the shelf and another register can take it.
Missing on the backend as well.

renderAlert: Draws one Types.Manager.ManagerAlert by constructor: low stock with item name, quantity and threshold; stale sale with its id and seconds open; register variance with its id.
Variance is expected minus counted. A positive figure is shown as short, a negative one as over.

decisions.name: RegistersAreManagedOnOnePage
decisions.what: Registers are created, opened, closed and chosen for this device here and nowhere else
why: Create is shown with capCanManageRegisters. Owner decision: only a manager or an admin creates a register. The backend enforces it.
Open is shown with capCanOpenRegister on a closed register and takes the starting cash. Close is shown with capCanCloseRegister on an open register and takes the counted cash.
A new register is closed. Creating and opening are separate steps, so a failed open cannot leave a half-made register behind an error.
'Use on this device' stores the register id through Services.RegisterService. The sale page sells on that register.

page: The list comes from API.Register.getRegisters and is read again after every action, accepted or refused.
One request runs at a time; submit buttons are disabled while busy and while the form is invalid.
A user who cannot manage registers and finds none is told to ask a manager.
Every register is created under Config.Entity.dummyLocationId.
describeVariance: Variance is expected minus counted, in cents. Zero matches, positive is short, negative is over.
cashForm: One dollar-amount field parsed by UI.Form.Parser.cents.
submit: Runs the action with the form's value only when the form is valid and no request is running.

openIssues.name: RegistersPageIsUnstyled
openIssues.what: The page uses class names that have no CSS rules yet
why: register-row, register-name, register-state, register-device, register-drawer, register-action, register-create, register-list, registers-page and register-needed.

decisions.name: OpenSaleIsRememberedPerUser
decisions.what: The id of the sale a user is working on is kept in localStorage under 'current_sale_id:<user id>'
why: A reload or a later sign-in by the same user continues the same sale.
The key used to be 'current_sale_id' for every user. On 2026-10-10 the backend log showed each sign-in reading the previous user's sale (GET /sale/<id>) before starting its own.
start remembers each sale under sale.saleEmployeeId, the opener the backend recorded, which is the session user.
The old shared key is no longer read or written. A value left under it in a browser is unused.

decisions.name: NothingHereStartsASaleOnItsOwn
decisions.what: A sale is started only by startOn and startNext, and the pages call both from a button
why: resumeOrStart used to start a sale whenever the sale page was opened without a resumable one. On 2026-10-10 that left empty open sales on the backend: one per sign-in, and one after each completed sale that was followed by a sign-out.
resumeOrStart was removed. resume only reads; Pages.CreateTransaction shows a Start Sale button when resume finds nothing.
Every started sale is an audited row (Transaction created) in the backend compliance log, so a sale nobody asked for is a false record.

resume: Sends no write. With nothing remembered for this user it returns Right Nothing without any request.
Right (Just sale) only when UI.Transaction.Model.canResume allows: still open, opened by this user, on this register.
A remembered sale that is gone (404) or can no longer be resumed gives Right Nothing and the remembered id is removed.
Any other failure to read the remembered sale gives Left and keeps the remembered id, because the sale may still be open.
Another user on the same browser has a different key and never reads the first user's sale.
startOn: Starts a sale on the given register and its location and remembers it. The backend records the session user as the opener.
startNext: Starts a sale on the register and location of the given sale and remembers it. The backend records the session user as the opener.

openIssues.name: OpenSaleFoundOnlyInTheSameBrowser
openIssues.what: A sale opened in another browser, or before localStorage was cleared, is not found and stays open on the backend
why: The backend has no route that returns a user's open sale; GET /sale returns every sale.
Such a sale shows as live in the manager's activity and later as a stale-transaction alert.
The user is then offered Start Sale and can open a second sale while the first is still open.
blocking: never leaving an open sale behind

openIssues.name: StartedSaleCanStillBeLeftEmpty
openIssues.what: A sale started with Start Sale or New Sale and then abandoned stays open and empty until its opener resumes it or a manager voids it
why: It is resumed the next time the same user opens the sale page in the same browser on the same register.
Wanted on both sides: create the sale with its first item, so that an empty sale cannot exist.

decisions.name: PagesRegisterCleanupWithOnLeave
decisions.what: OnLeave is a function a page calls with a close action; Main runs every registered action before the next render, including on sign-out
why: This version of Deku has no unmount hook, so a page cannot close its own stream when it is replaced.
Used by Pages.Stock.Interface, Pages.Admin.Tabs.LogViewer and Pages.Admin.Tabs.FeedMonitor.
The module holds only the type alias OnLeave = Effect Unit -> Effect Unit and no functions.
